svg.title: Groups and commands in time
svg.text: R1 and R2 in flight together: their groups share no core
R3's group overlaps both: the cores it shares with R1 or R2 take it after their first command, core 5 at once. This order is
the drawn case, not a guarantee: a shared core may run two commands in flight in either order, unless the later is exclusive.
an X280 thread runs the rounds; the host sends one command
to the cores this round gives spin

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: Each round the thread reads the round's amounts, chooses k, submits both commands and waits. 24 rounds on 120 cores:
1,023 µs with the thread's split, 7,521 µs with the host feeding a fixed split round by round.
a leader casts which code its group runs next

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: The leader picks from a value it reads; every core of the broadcast, the leader too, loads the overlay if it does not hold it, and calls it.
a command lands on every core; cores outside its group skip it
a command submitted, or acknowledged by its leader
